intro.t: After what they share, say how they're different. That's what turns a description into a comparison. Six ways to do it.

close.t: Well done. Share, then differ. That's the shape of every Part 2 minute.

ex.t: {The main difference is that} the people in the first photo are working as a team.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be difficult for the people in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A group of colleagues in a meeting around an office table · Photo 2: Someone working alone on a laptop in a café

ex.t: {The main difference is that} the market looks much more personal than the mall.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be enjoyable or frustrating about shopping in these places.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A big, modern shopping mall with lots of stores · Photo 2: A local market with individual stalls

ex.t: {The main difference is that} football is a team sport, but in the gym it's just you.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what skills the people might be developing through these activities.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A team playing football together on a field · Photo 2: Someone working out alone in a gym

reels.note: Moves your eyes to the second picture.

ex.t: {Unlike the first one,} the library looks calm and quiet.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say how the people might be feeling in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A crowded city street at night, full of lights and people · Photo 2: A group of students studying together in a library

ex.t: {Unlike the first one,} the second photo shows someone alone in nature.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might make these travel experiences memorable for the people.
ex.scene: Photo 1: Tourists visiting famous buildings and landmarks in a city · Photo 2: Someone on an adventure in nature, by a lake in the mountains

ex.t: {Unlike the first one,} the person in the café seems to be working alone.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be difficult for the people in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A group of colleagues in a meeting around an office table · Photo 2: Someone working alone on a laptop in a café

reels.note: The favourite of B2 candidates. Both halves in one sentence.

ex.t: The cinema is quite quiet, {whereas} the family at home can chat and laugh.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have chosen to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: People watching a film in a cinema · Photo 2: A family playing a board game together at home

ex.t: The beach looks relaxing, {whereas} hiking in the mountains looks quite tiring.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have decided to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A peaceful beach at sunset · Photo 2: Someone hiking in the mountains

ex.t: The students are studying on their own, {whereas} the children have a parent helping them.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what the people might be learning from these experiences.
ex.scene: Photo 1: University students studying together in a library · Photo 2: A parent at home helping young children with a tablet

reels.note: Starts the second half as its own sentence.

ex.t: The mall has everything in one place. {On the other hand,} the market is more fun.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be enjoyable or frustrating about shopping in these places.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A big, modern shopping mall with lots of stores · Photo 2: A local market with individual stalls

ex.t: Team sports teach you to work together. {On the other hand,} the gym is more flexible.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what skills the people might be developing through these activities.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A team playing football together on a field · Photo 2: Someone working out alone in a gym

ex.t: The beach is easy to get to. {On the other hand,} the mountains feel more like an adventure.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have decided to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A peaceful beach at sunset · Photo 2: Someone hiking in the mountains

reels.note: Short, strong, always at the start of a sentence.

ex.t: Going to the cinema can be expensive. {However,} playing a board game at home is free.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say why the people might have chosen to spend their time in these ways.
ex.scene: Photo 1: People watching a film in a cinema · Photo 2: A family playing a board game together at home

ex.t: A library is good for concentrating. {However,} learning at home might feel more relaxed.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what the people might be learning from these experiences.
ex.scene: Photo 1: University students studying together in a library · Photo 2: A parent at home helping young children with a tablet

ex.t: City tours can be crowded. {However,} the lake in the mountains looks really peaceful.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might make these travel experiences memorable for the people.
ex.scene: Photo 1: Tourists visiting famous buildings and landmarks in a city · Photo 2: Someone on an adventure in nature, by a lake in the mountains

reels.note: Then you can add smaller differences after it.

ex.t: {The most obvious difference is} the noise. The street must be really loud.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say how the people might be feeling in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A crowded city street at night, full of lights and people · Photo 2: A group of students studying together in a library

ex.t: {The most obvious difference is} the place: an office and a café.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what might be difficult for the people in these situations.
ex.scene: Photo 1: A group of colleagues in a meeting around an office table · Photo 2: Someone working alone on a laptop in a café

ex.t: {The most obvious difference is} the age of the learners.
ex.q: Compare the two photographs and say what the people might be learning from these experiences.
ex.scene: Photo 1: University students studying together in a library · Photo 2: A parent at home helping young children with a tablet
